title: Auction Tactics for Our 200 USD Live Draft
markdown:
**Summary.** At 12 teams with 144 players drafted, go balanced. Plan about 185 USD for 11 core players in roughly the rank 25 to 75 range, hold about 14 USD in reserve, and keep one 1 USD streaming spot. Use the first 10 nominations to read the room, vary your bidding, enforce prices only up to your own number, and treat mock and Yahoo prices as rough guides.

## Why balanced beats stars and scrubs at 12 teams

League size decides the build. The guidance is stars and scrubs in 8-team leagues, maybe in 10-team leagues, and balanced in anything bigger. We have 12 teams, so we go balanced. The deeper the league, the worse stars and scrubs works. Stars cost more and the 1 USD players get worse. A 12-team league has about 120 starting-level players, and we draft 144. So the last players bought in our room are below starting level. ([09-29](https://youtu.be/XnIWJyBB0EM?t=2404), [09-29](https://youtu.be/XnIWJyBB0EM?t=1670), [09-29](https://youtu.be/XnIWJyBB0EM?t=1841), [09-28](https://youtu.be/3Qm5wLjhvTw?t=1414))

Stars and scrubs carries two risks. First, a 1 USD player has only about a 10% chance of turning into a 10 to 15 USD player. Second, if one of your two stars gets hurt, the team is ruined. In our head-to-head format, a week with one star out is usually a lost week. Paying 80 USD each for two superstars is too much to win the league. In a balanced build, losing your best player hurts less. Replacing the 30th best player from waivers is much easier than replacing Jokic. ([09-29](https://youtu.be/XnIWJyBB0EM?t=1708), [10-05](https://youtu.be/Q6YlQDvD-aY?t=6391), [10-05](https://youtu.be/Q6YlQDvD-aY?t=445), [09-29](https://youtu.be/XnIWJyBB0EM?t=1809))

The balanced target: skip the projected top 20 and put your 11 core players in roughly ranks 25 to 75. The ceiling is lower, but the team is much safer. The market helps. Rooms tend to overpay for the top end and underpay for the middle. Be ready to finish the draft without a first-round player. Expect at least one other manager to go balanced and bid up mid-round bargains, so do not wait too long on the middle tier. ([09-29](https://youtu.be/XnIWJyBB0EM?t=1793), [09-04](https://youtu.be/gerS7ibpaJo?t=780), [10-05](https://youtu.be/Q6YlQDvD-aY?t=1040), [09-29](https://youtu.be/XnIWJyBB0EM?t=2365))

The experts disagree on how strict to be. One view says you can build a good team around two expensive stars, as long as you accept there is no margin for error. The same notes say to always adapt to value: if a star falls well below his price because the room went balanced, buy him. The other view says that above 10 teams you should simply go balanced. Our rule: start balanced by default. Buy a star only at a clear discount, never at full price. ([10-05](https://youtu.be/Q6YlQDvD-aY?t=6391), [09-29](https://youtu.be/XnIWJyBB0EM?t=2414), [09-29](https://youtu.be/XnIWJyBB0EM?t=2404), [09-29](https://youtu.be/XnIWJyBB0EM?t=1793))

The real goal is value, not a shape. Aim to get at least 250 USD of value from 200 USD. Getting players who finish well above their cost is the biggest factor in winning a league. No player is a must-have. Do not pay inflated punt prices because a player fits your build. Do not pay extra because you are a fan. For each bid, ask whether the price assumes his best-case outcome or his typical one. ([09-29](https://youtu.be/XnIWJyBB0EM?t=1079), [09-22](https://youtu.be/QbdrhJd7LiA?t=2026), [09-17](https://youtu.be/ahNxsoU8Hx4?t=110), [09-28](https://youtu.be/3Qm5wLjhvTw?t=566), [09-29](https://youtu.be/XnIWJyBB0EM?t=913), [10-05](https://youtu.be/Q6YlQDvD-aY?t=946), [07-17](https://youtu.be/NYTH7uQsPCM?t=294))

## Budget split and the streaming spot

Do not budget for all 12 spots. Keep at least one spot for streaming and fill it for 1 USD. A streaming spot is worth about a top 100 to 110 player. Our daily lineups and daily FAB waivers make streaming practical. The weekly limit is 6 acquisitions, so plan your adds. ([09-29](https://youtu.be/XnIWJyBB0EM?t=408), [10-05](https://youtu.be/Q6YlQDvD-aY?t=4744))

Our split: plan about 185 USD for 11 core players, keep about 14 USD of wiggle room, and spend 1 USD on the streaming spot. That works out to roughly 17 USD per core player on average. The wiggle room is not savings. It exists to win bargains later. If you finish with money unspent, you planned the budget wrong. ([09-29](https://youtu.be/XnIWJyBB0EM?t=488), [09-29](https://youtu.be/XnIWJyBB0EM?t=589), [10-05](https://youtu.be/Q6YlQDvD-aY?t=4744))

Build decision trees by player shape, not by name. If you miss a target, or get one cheaper than planned, move that money to another slot. Keep a clear backup in your queue so a snipe does not make you panic. Do not set rigid position or stat targets for each stage. Plans break once bidding starts. Fill positions, and watch which categories are about to run out. ([09-29](https://youtu.be/XnIWJyBB0EM?t=573), [09-30](https://youtu.be/BjXP9JODDSg?t=1881), [09-23](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=2541), [09-24](https://youtu.be/_vbAP5y182A?t=947), [09-01](https://youtu.be/skKXe2CRl8Q?t=626))

After every win, recheck how much you can spend per open slot. Keep back 1 USD for each slot you plan to fill at the minimum. Spending everything early locks you out of the late bargains. ([10-05](https://youtu.be/Q6YlQDvD-aY?t=2873), [09-29](https://youtu.be/XnIWJyBB0EM?t=589))

## Reading a hot or cold room

Nominate big names early. This takes cash off the board, and the first prices tell you whether the room is hot or cold. Watch the first 10 or so nominations closely. In nearly every draft, one of them goes well under value. After that, the room pushes up later prices. Once one player goes well under his expected price, everyone's thinking changes and the rest of the draft shifts. ([10-05](https://youtu.be/Q6YlQDvD-aY?t=318), [09-29](https://youtu.be/XnIWJyBB0EM?t=1181), [09-26](https://youtu.be/3UGI05PDvrE?t=1794))

Hot room: the top players go above projections. Money spent above projections has to come out of other players' prices, so later prices will dip. Do not chase the top. Switch to a cheaper balanced build, target mid-round value, and wait. Late in a hot draft, real value appears if you are patient. ([09-29](https://youtu.be/XnIWJyBB0EM?t=1010), [10-05](https://youtu.be/Q6YlQDvD-aY?t=568), [10-05](https://youtu.be/Q6YlQDvD-aY?t=622), [10-05](https://youtu.be/Q6YlQDvD-aY?t=3542))

Cold room: the top players go below expected prices. Managers still have money, so mid-round prices will rise. This is when buying a discounted star makes sense, because your planned mid-round targets will get more expensive anyway. ([09-29](https://youtu.be/XnIWJyBB0EM?t=1026), [09-29](https://youtu.be/XnIWJyBB0EM?t=2414))

## Nominations, bidding style and price enforcement

Mix up your nominations. Nominate players you do not want, so other teams spend money that could have gone to your targets. Early on, nominate players you see as 1 USD guys. Others will often pay 4 or 5 USD for them. Do not nominate your real targets while the other managers have the most money. ([09-29](https://youtu.be/XnIWJyBB0EM?t=1181), [09-29](https://youtu.be/XnIWJyBB0EM?t=1230), [10-05](https://youtu.be/Q6YlQDvD-aY?t=3753))

Vary your bidding style. Sometimes bid quickly, sometimes drain the timer, and sometimes drop out. If you are predictable, sharp drafters will use it against you. ([09-29](https://youtu.be/XnIWJyBB0EM?t=1400))

Use price enforcement to make opponents pay up for players they want. Only push to a price where you would be happy to get stuck with the player, because sometimes you will. Know when to stop. If an opponent is about to overpay in a way that hurts him for the rest of the draft, let him have the player. A player you do not like can still be a good buy if he is cheap enough, so judge every price against consensus value, not personal bias. ([09-29](https://youtu.be/XnIWJyBB0EM?t=1532), [10-05](https://youtu.be/Q6YlQDvD-aY?t=2162), [09-09](https://youtu.be/7BllEsdNLoM?t=2066), [10-02](https://youtu.be/ZYllcj4o6_A?t=322))

## The 1 USD endgame

Late in the draft, track each manager's max bid. A team with a few extra dollars can snipe the 1 USD player you are waiting on. Do not hang everything on one sleeper. Keep a flexible list with large groups of similar targets, so losing one costs you nothing. With 144 players drafted and about 120 starting-level players, most of the endgame pool is streaming level anyway. ([10-05](https://youtu.be/Q6YlQDvD-aY?t=5613), [09-29](https://youtu.be/XnIWJyBB0EM?t=1273), [09-28](https://youtu.be/3Qm5wLjhvTw?t=1414))

Your reserve pays off here. The market can overreact to an injury tag and leave value on the board. If you kept money back, you can bid 2 or 3 USD on these players while the other teams are stuck at 1 USD. ([10-05](https://youtu.be/Q6YlQDvD-aY?t=2546), [09-29](https://youtu.be/XnIWJyBB0EM?t=589), [10-05](https://youtu.be/Q6YlQDvD-aY?t=3542))

## Mock prices and Yahoo prices are only guides

Auction prices change with any settings change: number of teams, roster size, categories, or the split between starters and bench. Prices from a 10-team mock, or one with a different roster, mean little for our 12-team, 9-category, 12-player room. Before the draft, check that your value sheet uses our settings and the 200 USD budget. Snake draft order carries over between leagues much better than auction prices do. ([09-29](https://youtu.be/XnIWJyBB0EM?t=300), [09-26](https://youtu.be/3UGI05PDvrE?t=1730), [09-26](https://youtu.be/3UGI05PDvrE?t=1814), [10-05](https://youtu.be/Q6YlQDvD-aY?t=48))

Yahoo average and projected prices are only guides, and your plan will get disrupted during the draft. Yahoo auction prices differ a lot from snake ADP, so do not convert one into the other. An average built from very few drafts can be inflated. Use the market price to judge what you will have to pay, and your own value to judge what a player is worth. If your value is well above the market price, you only need to bid a little above the market. ([09-29](https://youtu.be/XnIWJyBB0EM?t=1036), [09-07](https://youtu.be/gJUBAJaHzlU?t=998), [10-03](https://youtu.be/_O9pc_u5vH0?t=1150), [09-01](https://youtu.be/skKXe2CRl8Q?t=579))

The experts disagree on mock auctions. One side says they can mislead more than they help, and that they do not carry over because the real room shifts after the first bargain. The other side says mocks have some use if you practice flexibility and try different paths, not repeat one pattern. Both sides agree that fixating on mock trends causes panic when the real draft goes differently. Early September mocks are mostly out of date by now anyway. With the draft on 2026-10-18, use any last mock to practice adapting, not to set prices. ([09-27](https://youtu.be/CRLSsoGhb2w?t=1934), [09-26](https://youtu.be/3UGI05PDvrE?t=1794), [09-30](https://youtu.be/BjXP9JODDSg?t=436), [09-25](https://youtu.be/Bi1cEM03k9Y?t=2073), [09-07](https://youtu.be/E-KmhvyZ2CU?t=1091), [09-25](https://youtu.be/4gw4W4RTolY?t=97))

<sub>Built 2026-10-16 with claude-opus-5-5 high.</sub>
